identity.name: Later Han (Five Dynasties)
alt_names: Later Han of the Five Dynasties

land.text: the Later Jin realm: the Later Han 'held essentially the same territory as the Later Jin'

predecessors.note: The infobox lists the Later Jin as the predecessor. The Later Jin fell to the Khitan on 11 January 947; Liu Zhiyuan proclaimed the Later Han at Taiyuan on 10 March 947.

land.text: the Central Plain the Khitan left: Emperor Taizong of Liao's force reached the Yellow River, then turned back toward his base near present-day Beijing

predecessors.note: The Sixteen Prefectures 'remained with the Liao'.

minus.text: the Later Han realm at its end
the Shanxi core where the Northern Han began: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

land.text: the Later Han realm without the Northern Han core in Shanxi (Guo Wei's realm at Kaifeng)

successors.note: Guo Wei's coup of 1-2 January 951 (infobox 'de facto end'); proclaimed emperor 13 February 951 ('de jure end').

land.text: the Shanxi core where the Northern Han began: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

successors.note: The Later Han page describes remnants returning to Shanxi to found the Northern Han kingdom.

capitals.name: Taiyuan
capitals.note: Infobox 'Established in Taiyuan: March 10, 947'. The infobox lists no capital years; Taiyuan is the seat until the move to Bian, which the page does not date by month.

capitals.name: Bian (Kaifeng)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capitals: Bian (Kaifeng)'; Liu Zhiyuan 'established his capital at Bian, present day Kaifeng'.

rulers.name: Yin (Liu Chengyou)
rulers.title: Emperor Yin
rulers.note: Killed on 2 January 951 in Guo Wei's coup (infobox).

correction.text: the shape unchanged but valid 947-950 only: on 1-2 January 951 'Coup d'etat, surrender of Bian; Emperor Yin killed (de facto end)'; the 951-959 years are the Later Zhou's (later-zhou_951) and the Northern Han's (northern-han_951)

keyframe_review.note: 790,319 km2, the same outline as Cliopatria's Later Jin 936 shape; the page gives no area but says the Later Han 'held essentially the same territory as the Later Jin', north over much of Shaanxi and Hebei except the Sixteen Prefectures, which remained with the Liao, south along a line about halfway between the Yellow and Yangtze rivers to the Yangtze's middle reaches, then northwest along the northern edge of Sichuan to Shaanxi (the page's description). The shape also contains the Northern Han's Shanxi core (the whole 26,506 km2 Northern Han shape lies inside it, checked by intersection). Cliopatria keeps the row to 959, nine years past the dynasty. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 947..950 from this entry's own 'valid 947-950 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: the Later Jin realm minus the Sixteen Prefectures

ledger.note: 947: Liu Zhiyuan takes over the Central Plain from the Khitan. The Liao force reached the Yellow River and then turned back; Liu 'established his capital at Bian, present day Kaifeng' and the Later Han 'held essentially the same territory as the Later Jin', except the Sixteen Prefectures. The page gives no month for the entry into Bian.
947: the Later Han capital moves from Taiyuan to Bian (Kaifeng). 'established his capital at Bian, present day Kaifeng'; the infobox lists only Bian. No month on the page.

region.text: Taiyuan, where Liu Zhiyuan proclaimed the dynasty as jiedushi

ledger.note: 10 March 947: Liu Zhiyuan proclaims the Later Han at Taiyuan. Infobox 'Established in Taiyuan: March 10, 947' (text: 'March 947'); Emperor Taizong of Liao died of illness in May 947, which led to a power vacuum that Liu Zhiyuan filled (the page's account).

region.text: the Shanxi core where the Northern Han began: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

ledger.note: 951: the Northern Han splits off in Shanxi. The Later Han page describes remnants returning to Shanxi to found the Northern Han kingdom; the Northern Han page: 'Liu Min founded the Northern Han Kingdom ... in 951', claiming 'that he was the legitimate heir to the imperial throne of Later Han'. No month on either page; it follows the January coup, so it is listed before the dissolve only because a missing month sorts first.

minus.text: the Later Han realm at its end
the Shanxi core where the Northern Han began: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

region.text: the Later Han realm without the Northern Han core in Shanxi (Guo Wei's realm at Kaifeng)

ledger.note: January 951: Guo Wei takes the realm at Kaifeng. Guo Wei, a Han Chinese, 'led a military coup and declared himself emperor of the Later Zhou'; infobox 'Coup d'etat, surrender of Bian; Emperor Yin killed (de facto end): January 1; January 2, 951'; 'Guo Wei proclaimed Emperor (de jure end): February 13 951'.

region.text: the Later Han realm at its end

ledger.note: 1-2 January 951: the Later Han ends in Guo Wei's coup. Infobox successors 'Later Zhou; Northern Han'; Emperor Yin (Liu Chengyou) killed on 2 January 951.

wars.name: Khitan withdrawal from the Central Plain and the rise of the Later Han

zones.text: the Central Plain as far as the Yellow River

wars.outcome: The Liao force that had taken Kaifeng reached the Yellow River and turned back; Taizong of Liao died in May 947 and Liu Zhiyuan filled the vacuum, keeping the Sixteen Prefectures with the Liao.
wars.note: The page gives no battle and no month for the Khitan withdrawal; the later-jin dossier dates the fall of Kaifeng to 11 January 947.

wars.name: Guo Wei's coup against the Later Han
wars.outcome: General Guo Wei seized Bian on 1-2 January 951 and was proclaimed emperor of the Later Zhou on 13 February 951; the Later Han remnants returned to Shanxi as the Northern Han.
wars.note: A coup, not a territorial war. The Northern Han page says the Later Han 'fell in 950 because of Guo Wei'; the Later Han infobox gives 1-2 January 951.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Later Han border; the page describes the south as a line 'about halfway between the Yellow and Yangtze rivers' and the northern frontier with the Liao follows the Sixteen Prefectures, which are not surveyed lines.

sources.title: Later Han (Five Dynasties)
sources.note: Infobox dates (10 March 947 to 1-2 January 951), capital Bian, rulers, 'held essentially the same territory as the Later Jin', the Khitan withdrawal, Guo Wei's coup; silent on area, circuits, rebellions.

sources.title: Northern Han

notes:
Later Han (Cliopatria 947-959, one shape, 790,319 km2, the same outline as the Later Jin's 936 shape). The state ran 947-951; the Cliopatria years 951-959 are the Later Zhou's (the later-zhou dossier carries them, keyframe later-zhou_951) and the Northern Han core (northern-han_951 new keyframe in the northern-han dossier). Cliopatria draws no Later Zhou shape for 951-959 and keeps this row instead.

Page budget: 2 pages opened (the Five Dynasties page is shared). Not on either page: the month of the entry into Kaifeng; the 947-950 rebellions (Li Shouzhen, Zhao Siyuan, Wang Jingchong) and any Later Shu loss of Qin/Feng; circuits and area; the date Liu Min proclaimed the Northern Han (the Later Han page does not name Liu Min or Liu Chong). Wikipedia dates: infobox 'Established in Taiyuan: March 10, 947', end 1-2 January 951 de facto and 13 February 951 de jure (the Later Zhou dossier starts in February 951); the Northern Han page says the Later Han 'fell in 950 because of Guo Wei'.

Identity: Cliopatria's Wikipedia field 'Later Han' is a disambiguation page (the Eastern Han is also called the Later Han); identity.wikipedia uses 'Later Han (Five Dynasties)'. The Later Han page lists Liu Zhiyuan's reign as 947-948 and Liu Chengyou's as 948-951. Mirrors wanted: later-jin (end 947), liao-dynasty (the 947 withdrawal), later-zhou (gain 951), northern-han (found 951).
